mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) in thousands of units consistently correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days, as increased residential construction activity signals robust consumer demand and economic expansion that supports equity valuations.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST level and 20-day S&P 500 returns is negative or statistically insignificant (p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window in historical data.

mechanism_narrative: A FEDFUNDS rate exceeding 4.5% triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days, as aggressive monetary tightening increases discount rates and reduces equity valuation multiples through higher risk-free rates.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in PAYEMS (employment) and decrease in UNRATE (unemployment) generates positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days, as labor market strength amplifies consumer spending power and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling fails to produce positive returns in more than 60% of instances, or the interaction term in a regression model is insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, a decline in INDPRO (industrial production) signals weakening supply capacity that triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days due to reduced corporate output and profit margins.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion, a declining INDPRO is followed by positive 20-day S&P 500 returns in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 240 (index) triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days, as persistent inflation pressures compel central banks to implement restrictive monetary policy that reduces equity attractiveness.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 240, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle recovery regimes, a rising RSAFS (retail sales) signals strengthening consumer demand that drives positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days through increased corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: In early-cycle recovery, a rising RSAFS is not followed by positive 20-day S&P 500 returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A higher HOUST level consistently correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days, as housing activity serves as a leading indicator of near-term consumer spending momentum.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST level and 5-day S&P 500 returns is negative or insignificant (p > 0.05) over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A FEDFUNDS rate exceeding 4.5% triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days, as prolonged monetary tightening suppresses economic growth and equity valuations through sustained higher discount rates.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances.
